title: The Hero's Journey
subtitle: You are the protagonist, the star, the hero! Trust me, no one can resist the spotlight.

content.text: In an old bookstore on Rue Saint-Honoré, a faded book draws your attention. Its contents are exactly what you want to understand. You brush your fingers once more across the gold-stamped title.
Salon Etiquette—Written by a Court Attendant

branch.text: Yes. A book that helps you blend into society.
Yes. A book that awakens the wild.
Yes. A book that lights two souls at once.
Yes. A book that questions the nature of the world.

trails.title: Not Every Story Ends in Joy

content.text: It was then that I decided to help Brume one last time.
There was risk in my choice. I could not see what the consequences would be.
Still, I succeeded, and the rewards were most generous. Many suspected that I had planned it from the start—a common accusation made of diviners, of course.
You chose to let the villain live.

branch.text: Do you think I did not punish her enough?
She lives, true, but sealed inside a false diamond. I doubt that was the life she had intended.
Besides, Brume has the right to decide her fate. It was not my place to choose whether she lives or dies.
Thank you for your concern; I am doing well, though the future now comes to me through an ever-thickening haze.
Though, I should say, I find myself welcoming the lack of clarity.
I am now able to watch my daughter grow, to observe her, and feel true surprise in every step she takes.
If there is anything to take away from Brume's story, I would suggest this:
Sometimes, good can come from being blind to fate's path.
How exciting it must be to arrive in this world knowing nothing and, after a long, beautiful journey, realize just how much there is still to discover.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Sounds like you're just trying to pass the burden onto me.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Whether she lives or dies ... The weight ends up on my shoulders, doesn't it?
The question is more direct than expected. Beryl thinks over the words, then nods again.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: In many ways you two are alike; neither of you can stand by as fate attempts to pull you down its path. You fight.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: It is no wonder that she could reach into the depths of your mind.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: Now, her very existence is in your hands. You will not have another chance like this.
She reaches out her hand.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: Your friend and the original Félicienne perished in the same way. It is likely, then, that she has returned to the Depths of Myth.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: Should Félicienne live, she may become the key to discovering the truth of that realm. And in time, you may even find a way to bring your friend back.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: Yet, should she die, you will have taken a fitting revenge, and her torment of your body will end at last.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Swear it, then. Swear that every word you just said is true.
One pair of earnest eyes meets another, calm and unflinching.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: You ask for something beyond what I am capable of.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: As you know, arcanum has its limits. There is no absolute way to prove one's intentions or words, just as I cannot see all ends as clearly as I once did.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: Time is ticking. Give me the diamond now, or lose this opportunity forever.
Adèle hesitates, then raises her arm.
Félicienne is silent, or perhaps she can no longer speak.
She lowers her head. That proud defiance she once carried is gone.
Irritation, exhaustion, and aimless rage wash over her. And in the end, it all becomes a sigh.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: ... Take it.
Her resentment is still there, but somehow looking at her broken and pathetic, it awakens some pity in her.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Save her.
The diamond drops into Beryl's palm.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: Thank you.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: You have led me to the answer. I will respond with the sincerity it deserves.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: As I have said before, your fates have converged.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: Félicienne, your journey through the spiritual realm has reached its end. But you still have a place in the crown of the material world.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: Now, the pneuma that has reached the edge of one world must begin anew in the next.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: Take this, Adèle.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: An accolade for your adventure.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Hah. An accolade?
It's back in her hand.
Stained with blood, warm with tears, the last thing she still owns.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Thank you.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: But your eyes ...

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: Please do not worry yourself.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: It seems I have walked this shoreline too long. I have grown too accustomed to watching its flow.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: The more I think I see through fate, the more vulnerable I become to it.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: Still, I chose to watch one final time—just this once.
She smiles and points to the diamond clutched in Adèle's hand.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: It makes for a fine "imitation."

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: Your flame separated the French Blue from the smoky quartz it had inhabited.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: I simply gave it a new vessel—a clear quartz. It was the best that I could manage. I hope it will suffice.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: And I hope both you and Félicienne will be satisfied with it.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Will she wake up soon? And when that happens, will I still see her image in my hallucinations like before?

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: You will suffer no more hallucinations.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: And she will awaken again—in time.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: Yet you will be the sole master of your body. She is but a soul quietly bound to it.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: So long as neither of you strays too far from the other, her soul should remain whole.
Its edges cut into her fingers. She feels the veins in her fingertips tighten, pulling at her heart.
Everything unfolds as foretold.
Even the French Blue fulfills its destined curse, entangling its bearer like a shadow.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: The rain is about to fall. We must go. By dawn tomorrow, this world will be washed clean.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: I must admit, I enjoyed this ending of yours. But whether you continue to the next chapter is up to you.
But when the show ends, the audience must leave.
Beryl has always obeyed that rule, and she is not about to change.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Madame Bouanich!

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Madame Bouanich, forgive me, do you know the theory of evolution?

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Humankind evolved from apes. I don't understand the science, but, in short, we all came from monkeys.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: But then, where did that monkey come from? Are we all just a copy of a copy of some ancient thing?

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: And if we keep tracing back, how did life even begin on Earth?

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Can we ever find that original spark of life? Is it even possible?

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: What I'm trying to say is, things rarely have a single clear cause.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: The birth of life is complex. It can be influenced by all kinds of factors.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Maybe that applies to fate as well.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: So, whatever happens, I don't intend for my story to end any time soon.
Friends, home, curses, prophecies ... Everything she's ever hoped for or fought to achieve means nothing against the rain.
If only one explanation remains, she'll seize it.
Even if it's just a fragile thread of silk.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Please, take me with you. There must be a way to avoid this "Storm" you spoke of!
She shouts—the Tavernier Curse may already be in motion.
This is the goal fate intended. A goal worth dying for. The rain washes everything away, ending her long wait.
As ordinary life fades away, her adventure truly begins.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: I'll help you find jewels in return—answers, anything! Whatever it is you seek!

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: A generous offer. To honor your sincerity, I shall give you an answer. What is it you wish to know?

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: The truth about the "Storm."
She answers without hesitation.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: I need to understand it so I can bring back my friends.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: Including Félicienne?

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: I wouldn't call her a friend. But for her to simply vanish, hmph, that's just too merciful for her.
The diviner listens to every word, then nods.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: Would you still accompany me, knowing we may gain nothing in the end?

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: I would.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: You can't just sit around waiting for something terrible to happen, can you?
The little dragon climbs onto her shoulder and spits out a fireball.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: Indeed. I suppose there will never be an age lacking those who chase gemstones and answers about their fate.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: Perhaps a jewel hunter is exactly what my little establishment needs.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Which way do we go, Madame Bouanich?

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: Forward. Through the crowd.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: Allow me to guide you.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: I'm just glad to be of service, madame.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: I hope you have a pleasant journey.
Beryl takes a final wistful look at the revelers.
This city is just the place where she keeps herself, a jewelry box made to hold a precious crystal.
Still, she decides to remember it—just a little longer. That's enough.
She leans back in the passenger seat and closes her eyes.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: For a long while going forward, I may not be able to divine with the same precision I once had.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: Yet this feeling of "not seeing" has a comfort of its own.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: If our fate truly is guided by a higher being, I must imagine they are blind.
The radio begins to play.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: I hope that, when I awake, you will have reached your destination.
